# iru_library_item_statuses (Data Source)

Reads a bounded, complete Library Item status snapshot for one exact UUID through GET only. Reports numeric status-record IDs, device/Blueprint UUIDs, opaque reported status and nullable reported timestamp; rows are sorted by status-record ID. Names, user identity, logs, EDR payloads and installer URLs are excluded. An empty list or status string is not proof of assignment placement, successful installation/execution, convergence or item absence. No action or wait-until-success is performed. Every page must succeed; errors preserve cached state rather than return a partial snapshot. Sensitive rows remain plaintext in state/JSON, so protect those files.

The documented endpoint is `GET /api/v1/library/library-items/{library_item_id}/status`.
Use an existing Library Item UUID and a token permitted to read that endpoint.
The data source follows all pages on that exact tenant origin and endpoint, with
a two-minute operation bound, 100-page/10,000-record limits and the existing
2 MiB per-response safety limit. A failed, malformed or inconsistent page fails
the read; a partial list is never returned. HTTP404 is an error, not an empty
snapshot or permission to recreate a Library Item.

`statuses` is sensitive because it relates reported status to device and Blueprint
identities. It is still plaintext in state and machine-readable JSON. Protect
those files; outputs derived from the rows must use `sensitive = true`. Device
names, Blueprint names, users, logs, control logs and EDR details are excluded.
`record_count` counts status records, not unique devices. Several records may refer to
the same device. Reported status strings are observations; they are not normalized
into an assumed success enum. Missing/null Blueprint and timestamp metadata stays
null; an explicitly empty timestamp stays empty.

Concurrent changes can yield a non-atomic view. Changing declared totals and
duplicate record IDs are rejected, but same-size replacements between pages
cannot be detected without a server snapshot/version contract.

An empty snapshot does not prove that the item exists, has no assignments, was
installed, is compliant or executed successfully. This is not a polling waiter,
Assignment Map graph reader or reconciliation permission. It never calls a write
endpoint, follows an installer URL or executes a device action.

## Example Usage


```terraform
data "iru_library_item_statuses" "example" {
  library_item_id = "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001"
}

output "reported_status_count" {
  value = data.iru_library_item_statuses.example.record_count
}

output "reported_statuses" {
  value     = data.iru_library_item_statuses.example.statuses
  sensitive = true
}
```


<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `library_item_id` (String) Exact existing Library Item UUID; not a device UUID or display name.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Canonical selected Library Item UUID.
- `record_count` (Number) Number of status records in the validated complete snapshot, not necessarily unique devices.
- `statuses` (Attributes List, Sensitive) Sensitive status-record projection, sorted by numeric ID. Multiple records for one device are retained. Empty means no records were returned; it is not a readiness assertion. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--statuses))

<a id="nestedatt--statuses"></a>
### Nested Schema for `statuses`

Read-Only:

- `blueprint_id` (String) Reported canonical Blueprint UUID, or null when absent/null. Not node placement or a managed assignment.
- `device_id` (String) Canonical UUID from the reported computer record.
- `id` (Number) Positive numeric status-record ID; not a Library Item or device ID.
- `reported_at` (String) Exact reported timestamp string, or null when absent/null. No freshness guarantee; an explicit empty string stays empty.
- `status` (String) Exact nonblank reported status string. Unknown status values are observations, not interpreted success states.
